headline: Drake Maye injury news hits like a sledgehammer after brutal Lions loss
morning_brew: I am still trying to process the absolute catastrophe that unfolded in Detroit yesterday. Watching the Patriots get dismantled 35-10 is bad enough on its own, but the news that Drake Maye is likely looking at a season-ending ankle injury is a total gut punch that I honestly do not know how we recover from. The defense couldn't stop a nosebleed for most of the afternoon, and losing our franchise quarterback on top of a blowout defeat just feels like the cruelest way to spend a Sunday. I watched the second half through my fingers like a horror movie, and it was clear that whatever momentum we had is effectively gone.

Looking at the bigger picture, this season is teetering on the edge of a collapse that is starting to feel real. When you are sitting at 5-5 and your most important player goes down, you have to wonder if the front office is already looking toward next year. The offensive line struggled all day to give Tommy DeVito any time, and when your starters cannot protect the pocket or move the chains, you are going to get buried by a team like the Lions every single time. It is a dark day in New England, and the talk radio lines are going to be absolute bedlam all week.

On a much brighter note, the C's put on a clinic at the Garden last night, hanging 131 points on Dallas and setting a franchise record for an opening-period lead. Jayson Tatum was locked in for 32 points in just 30 minutes, and the whole squad looked like they were playing on a different planet. We are back at TD Garden tonight for a matchup with Orlando, and after seeing that level of dominance, I expect the boys to keep the foot on the gas. It is a quick turnaround, but watching this team play right now is the only thing keeping my blood pressure from hitting the ceiling.

news_digest.headline: Sources: Patriots fear Drake Maye has broken ankle
news_digest.dans_take: If this is season-ending, it basically pulls the rug out from under everything we were building toward.

news_digest.headline: Celtics set franchise record for largest lead at end of a first period
news_digest.dans_take: That first quarter was pure basketball nirvana and the exact kind of statement we needed.

trend_watch.trend: Tatum dropped 32 points on 11-of-18 shooting and added six assists in only 30 minutes of action.
trend_watch.dans_take: He was absolutely clinical last night and made that Dallas defense look like they were lost in the North End.

trend_watch.trend: The unit allowed multiple pressures all afternoon and struggled to open any lanes for the rushing attack.
trend_watch.dans_take: If they don't tighten up and start winning the line of scrimmage, we might as well just pack it in for the year.

trend_watch.trend: DeVito finished with 81 yards on 12-of-24 passing with one touchdown and an interception in the loss.
trend_watch.dans_take: It is a tough spot for anyone to step into, but the lack of rhythm was absolute torture to witness.
